title: FxConfig
description: One web-authored PROJECTILE or VFX library entry, as its own reusable entity: its art (a 'projectile'/'fx'-kind entry in the shared web library) plus, for a projectile, the ProjectileSpec tuning that entry ships with. The counterpart of EnemyConfig for the other two sheet kinds — see Web/RedMagicWeb/modules/fx-form.js.
$comment:
WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IS NOT. Before this schema a projectile/VFX library entry was sprites only: its numbers lived on whatever consumed it (EnemyStats ▸ Tuning ▸ projectile, a BossAttack's embedded ProjectileSpec). That is still true at RUNTIME and this file does not change it — see the 'projectile' property's $comment. What this document adds is an AUTHORING-side default carried by the entry itself, so 'FireOrb' can be defined once with the speed/lifetime/pierce it is supposed to have instead of those numbers being retyped into every enemy and boss attack that throws it.

FIELD NAMES ARE NOT INVENTED. The 'projectile' block is projectile-config.schema.json#/definitions/projectileSpec by $ref, unchanged — the exact eleven fields ProjectileConfigImporter already reads. In particular 'damage', 'count', 'knockbackMultiplier' and 'hitLayers' are NOT here, for the reason projectile-config.schema.json's own SCOPE CORRECTION note gives: they are per-shot arguments the attacker supplies (EnemyAttack.Shoot passes tuning.attackDamage / tuning.attackKnockbackMultiplier into ProjectileFactory.Spawn) or arrive via AbilityContext, so a value written here would be silently overwritten on every single shot. How many projectiles a volley fires is likewise the ATTACK's shape (BulletHellAttack's pattern/count, the weapon system's ShapeModifier), never a property of one projectile.

kind.description: Which of the two this document configures. 'fx' hides every projectile-only field.
kind.$comment: Narrowed from the shared enum rather than pinned with a 'const' like EnemyConfig's: one form authors both, and the two differ only by whether a ProjectileSpec comes along. The shared $ref still defines the vocabulary so the kinds cannot drift apart.

name.$comment: Same shape and the same reason as EnemyConfig.enemyName — FxPrefabBuilder.SafeName() already sanitizes the manifest's name into exactly this alphabet, so enforcing it at authoring time means what you type is what the asset is called.

libraryId.description: Id of the 'projectile'/'fx'-kind entry in the web library whose frames are this entity's art.
libraryId.$comment: The SAME id ProjectileSpec.libraryId carries, so an EnemyConfig that references this projectile and this document agree on one identifier. Optional only so a config can be inspected before its art is picked; the exporter always writes it, and FxPrefabBuilder.FindSourceFolder(libraryId) is what turns it into frames on disk.

projectile.description: The ProjectileSpec this entry ships with. Projectile-kind only.
projectile.$comment: AUTHORING DEFAULT, NOT THE LIVE TUNING. ProjectileFactory.Spawn calls Projectile.Configure/ConfigureBehaviour with the spec of whoever fired the shot on every single shot, so what actually flies in game is EnemyStats ▸ Tuning ▸ projectile (or the BossAttack's own embedded spec) — never the prefab's serialized fields. That is the enemy-projectile-tuning-lives-on-enemystats convention and this schema does not bend it. These values are (a) what the web form seeds an enemy's/boss's spec with when that projectile is picked, and (b) what ProjectileMovementPlaceholder uses to fly the prefab on its own in a scene with nothing firing it, which is the standalone Play-mode check. The 'prefab' key inside this block is meaningless here and should be omitted: the prefab is what this document BUILDS.

allOf.$comment: A VFX has no ProjectileSpec: nothing spawns it as a projectile, so speed/pierce/homing would be inert fields inviting someone to tune them.

movementMode.description: How the projectile is meant to travel. Only 'Straight' is implemented today; the rest are declared so a config can already say what it wants.
movementMode.$comment: DECLARED AHEAD OF ITS BEHAVIOUR, ON PURPOSE. Mirrors RedMagic.Gameplay.ProjectileMovementPlaceholder.MovementMode (Assets/Scripts/Gameplay/ProjectileMovementPlaceholder.cs), which FxPrefabBuilder stamps onto the built prefab. Today every mode flies straight — the placeholder implements 'Straight' and nothing else, and a non-Straight value is carried and logged, never silently treated as Straight-forever. The point of naming the other four now is that the real movers (BoomerangMovement, BounceMovement, SplitOnImpact…) become a DROP-IN: the config and the prefab already say which one they want, so shipping one is adding a component that reads this field, with no schema change, no re-export of existing entries and no importer rework. Enum member NAMES, never ordinals, so reordering this list cannot repoint an existing config.
